portola-names-tree.title: Portolá expedition camps on San Francisquito Creek, beside the site of the later "El Palo Alto" redwood
portola-names-tree.dateNote: Camped 6-11 November 1769 (Palóu, Costansó and Wikipedia agree on the dates).
portola-names-tree.revisionNote: The manuscript says the Portolá expedition named the redwood El Palo Alto in November 1769. No 1769 expedition diary reachable here (Portolá's own, Costansó's, or Palóu's Memoirs account of the same days) mentions a tree at the San Francisquito Creek camp or gives it a name. The first Spanish description of the great redwood at that crossing is Palóu's own 1774 diary, written when he came back to the place and noted that Portolá's party had camped there in 1769. Wikipedia's El Palo Alto article says the earliest known use of the name 'Palo Alto' is 1853 (the tree was first called Palos Colorados). So the sources support 'the expedition camped here in November 1769', not 'the expedition (or Portolá, or Crespí) named the tree'. Wikipedia's Palo Alto, California article does say the tree was 'sighted and named by the Portolá expedition in 1769'; that conflicts with the El Palo Alto article and with the diaries, and gives no primary source.
portola-names-tree.note: Who named the tree is not documented in the primary diaries. A 'Portolá named it' tradition exists (repeated in Wikipedia's Palo Alto article) but the 1769 diaries do not show it, and the name is first attested in 1853. Whether the tree standing today is the one the expedition camped under is itself doubted (the El Palo Alto article reports a local historian's view that the camp may have been under another tree downstream).
